To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
conditioned medium from cultured colorectal cancer cells affects peripheral blood mononucleated cells inflammatory phenotype in vitro.
conditioned media from Caco- 2 cells can induce inflammatory phenotypes in monocytes.

secreted cytokine and soluble factors from colorectal cancer cells (Caco2) induced the differentiation of peripheral blood mononucleated cells, particularly monocytes, toward an inflammatory phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of conditioned medium of cultured CRC cells on the inflammatory phenotype of monocytes.
the role of secreted cytokines in the tumor microenvironment and their impact on the immune response.
the effects of secreted factors from CRC cells on PBMCs, and it may help us to better understand the role of immune system in CRC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conditioned medium from CRC cell lines affects the immune responses of monocytes and macrophages in vitro, but the exact mechanism and the effect on the immune responses in vivo remain unclear.
the conditioned medium from Caco- 2 cells can affect the immune response of PBMCs and monocytes in vitro.
the secreted factors from Caco2 could affect immune cells, particularly the mononuclear ones, toward inflammatory phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conditioned media of CRC cells could be used to study the effect of tumor cells on immune cells and to develop novel therapeutic strategies for CRC patients.
conditioned media of Caco-2 cells may affect the immune response of peripheral blood mononucleocytes.
the secreted factors from CRC cells could affect immune responses in PBMCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inflammatory response is not only a consequence of cancer, but can also be an important contributor to the progression of cancer.
the secreted soluble factors from CACO-2 cells can affect the phenotype of immune cells.
CRC cell lines can influence immune cells and their functions.
